notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (7 in total). None found a statement by Fitzpatrick on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, a pause or slowdown, an agreement with China, or AI safety. Earlier attempt (searches refused) had checked his official press release list directly (fitzpatrick.house.gov/press-releases, pages 1 to 21 of 126, 15 Dec 2024 to 10 Nov 2026, titles only); only the 8 Apr 2026 AFL-CIO AI principles release mentions AI. I re-opened that release this time and confirmed the quoted sentence and the 8 April 2026 date. The quote is attributed jointly to Fitzpatrick and Kelly ('the lawmakers'), not to Fitzpatrick alone. The same release says the effort reflects his commitment to 'ensuring America leads the world in artificial intelligence with both strength and responsibility' (narrator wording, not his quote; left out). Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538): the fastdemocracy.com bill page (opened) lists 12 cosponsors, all Democrats; Fitzpatrick is not among them. congress.gov was not checked (returned 403 in the earlier attempt), so a later cosponsorship cannot be fully ruled out. Checked City & State PA, 14 Sep 2026, 'Pennsylvania politicians react to calls for an AI development slowdown': it does not mention Fitzpatrick. Other AI items found but outside the date range or not about catastrophic risk: 2024 Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act (co-introduced, May 2024); a legislative tracker lists him as co-sponsor of the CREATE AI Act of 2025 (H.R. 2381), not confirmed on an official page and not about catastrophic risk. Left out: the 16 Sep 2026 release on shielding ratepayers from data center costs (his quoted words do not mention AI; level D under ruling 5 anyway). No House letter about AI risk led by him was found (the many-signer August and September 2026 letters were not searched, per instructions). Hearing remarks, floor speeches and interviews were covered only as far as the web searches reached.
